sentences.text: Researchers used fruit flies engineered to carry human Alzheimer's disease genes specifically in their glial cells to investigate the gut-brain connection. Flies treated with antibiotics to remove their gut bacteria exhibited worse inflammation, cell death, and accumulation of Alzheimer's-related proteins compared to normal flies, alongside impaired sleep cycles, movement, and learning abilities.

The study found that Alzheimer's disease alters the types and amounts of specific bacteria living in the gut of these flies. The authors conclude that losing gut bacteria worsens Alzheimer's disease in these flies by disrupting inflammation, metabolism, and protein cleanup systems, noting that negative effects varied across different genetically modified fly types.
